PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. THORNDIKE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL HALLWAY - DAY

lines.text: YOUNG EMERSON COD, AGED 11, sits in a wooden chair by a closed
door, looking nervous.
Young Emerson Cod is 11 years, 2 months, 8
days and 3 hours old.
A door next to him opens and a stern-looking MALE TEACHER leans
out, motions for him to enter. Young Emerson takes a breath,
stands and goes in the door.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He is in big trouble.
As the door shuts, we see the lettering on the frosted glass for
the first time: “PRINCIPAL’S OFFICE.”
Young Emerson sits in the middle of an oversized couch, staring
ahead as the male teacher stands and talks to the O.S. principal
(behind camera).
In this case, the bigness was made slightly
less big by the fact of its tedious regularity.
For this was his 6th visit in 10 days.
Young Emerson in different clothes. A DIFFERENT TEACHER FADES
IN, matching position, taking over the explanation to the unseen
principal. ALSO FADING IN, another 11-YEAR-OLD BOY with a black
eye and a bandaged nose.
The previous Tuesday had seen Young Emerson
punch future frat boy and current lunch money
extorter, Guy Baxter.
A red-faced FEMALE TEACHER addresses the principal.
Wednesday saw the return of Young Emerson to
the Big Couch for the crime of inappropriate,
intentional double entandre during the
science fair.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
The female teacher turns around a poster-board display with the
headline: “RINGS DISCOVERED AROUND URANUS. Scientists plan
probes.”
The following Monday had seen two more
visits. One for the vulgar use of a dead
language and the second after a second
encounter with Guy Baxter.
Guy, sullen again, now has two black eyes.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Young Emerson assured everyone that he would
leave Guy alone now, as the bully had no
more eyes.
Emerson remains silent, but a small satisfied grin breaks
through...
As SPECIALISTS BEGIN TO FADE IN and surround the young man,
talking animatedly with one another as he sits quietly, staring
straight ahead.
Specialists were summoned, tests given,
therapies administered. A boy of above-
average intelligence who, previously, had
nothing but respect for rules and regulations,
Young Emerson’s sudden proclivity for mischief
remained an utter mystery.
CAMERA BEGINS TO TRACK BACK, away from the gaggle...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
An utter mystery to everyone but Young Emerson
himself...
As we PASS BACK across the top of a large desk to a graceful set
of folded HANDS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...because what troubled him was not parental
alienation or sublimated anger.
EMERSON’S POV of the crowd of specialists...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was a heart that felt as overstuffed as the
couch on which he sat. He was in love.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
The crowd parts, REVEALING PRINCIPAL SWINDLE, elegant, beautiful
and calm. The COMMOTION starts to SLO-MO as she locks eyes with
Young Emerson and allows herself the smallest of smiles...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
That 6th-grade year, Young Emerson learned
his most important lesson from Principal
Eleanor Swindle.

scenes.heading: INT. THORNDIKE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL HALLWAY - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: As the door opens and Emerson is shown out by the first MALE
TEACHER. The door shuts behind him.
Love makes you stupid.
He smiles, turns and PULLS a nearby FIRE ALARM and sits back
down on the chair to wait. As the door opens again and the
principal sternly motions for him to come back in...
RANDY MANN ENTERS to find himself in the BUSY MORNING RUSH of
Pie Hole customers. CHUCK, carrying a big tray of dirty dishes,
sees him looking around a bit lost, approaches...
Randy Mann, what brings you in out of the cold?
I think we’re in for a mid-winter thaw.
Normally, in the mornings, I can see my
breath from under my covers, which is kinda
daunting, ‘cause I sleep in the nude. But at
least I know if I cocoon myself in the
comforter and hop to the bathroom--
(notices her load)
Can I help you with those?
I’ll be okay if there’s a satisfying and
unexpected point to this story.
I couldn’t see my breath this morning.
(Chuck sinks under the
weight)
And I’m looking for Olive.
Now we’re talking.
(calls to the kitchen)
Olive. You have a gentleman caller come in
out of the thaw.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
OLIVE turns out of the STEAMING espresso machine, busy with the
coffee--
A whatidy-what what?
(notices Randy)
Randy? Hi.
(to Chuck)
Can I...?
Go.
Olive smiles nervously. As she moves off to talk with Randy,
NED comes out from the kitchen, ends up with Chuck behind the
counter.
Randy’s back.
To see Olive. In an awkward, “I was nowhere
near your neighborhood so I thought I’d stop
by” kind of way. It’s sweet.
They watch as Randy and Olive nervously flirt-talk.
I’m happy. Olive’s been through a tough
patch that I may have made tougher. And by
“may have” I mean “definitely did.” I want
this to work out with Randy.
(then)
And what better place to nurture romance
than the Pie Hole? Warmth, pie and snuggly
booths -- all the right ingredients.
Love doesn’t need “all the right ingredients.”
It’s heartier than that.
(off his smile)
What?
You just said love was “heartier.”
It is hearty. Look at ours -- it’s like those
blind fish that live in volcanos at the bottom
of the ocean. And we’re two fish that can’t
even touch.
‘Cause normally, fish are all over each other.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED: (2)
(giggles, then)
Our love has grown and survived in spite of
everything we’ve been through.
We have been through a lot.
(toasts with a coffee cup)
Here’s to us -- for successfully navigating
some extremely rough and complicated seas.
And here’s to Olive and Randy. May they have
smooth sailing ahead.
(arriving)
Cheers. What are we toasting?
You and-- Why is Randy leaving?
We decided to call it quits. Too much, too
soon. Actually, it was just me. Singular.
So, more accurately, I’d say it was me decided
to call it quit. I’ll be in the kitchen
rationalizing my panic attack.
And she exits to the kitchen. They see Randy heading out the
front door...
Man overboard.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - BOOTH - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Chuck sits with Randy.
Randy, you know that when people are nervous,
sometimes it’s easy to misunderstand what
they mean.
It was all fine, then suddenly she said,
“Goodbye,” and, “Thanks for coming,” and shook
my hand. Felt like closure to me.
It’s hard for Olive. She’s just come through
a sticky swamp of emotion and she doesn’t want
to get stuck again.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
I know all about her getting stuck on Ned. But
she said she’s over it. And maybe I’m under-
thinking this, but we seem to like each other.
But it’s scary starting something new. It’s
about exposing your heart to a stranger. And
putting your faith in the idea of someone, way
before you ever really know the truth about who
they are. It’s like driving a car blindfolded --
you have to relax.
“Relax”?
Ned talks with Olive.
“Relax”?
Maybe bullfighting’s the wrong comparison.
But it’s hard making these things work.
You are telling me these things are hard to
make work? I know they’re hard because you
taught me.
Maybe that’s why Randy’s scary to you --
because you’re not used to something that’s...
easy, and maybe really great.
(thinks, then)
Oh, my God. I’m that girl. I’m that girl in
high school who’s afraid of a real
relationship, so she’s always attracted to
guys in college or Canada.
(then)
Or... you.
I want you to be happy, Olive.
So, what you’re saying is that I shouldn’t run
away from Randy.
Yes.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
That Randy might be just what I need right now.
Yes.
A quick fling. That I can use to heal the
scars and rub ointment on the burns from us,
then peel off and toss out like a used square
of gauze.
Not yes.
He’s Randy Rebound.
No, he’s not.
As the Pie-Maker began to doubt his plan to
reunite the would-be lovers, a mile to the
West, another reunion was taking place.
EMERSON enters. His desk chair swivels around to REVEAL SIMONE
HUNDIN and BUBBLEGUM. He makes a move toward her -- she CLICKS
her clicker.
Stay.
Simone Hundin, breeder of well-heeled dogs,
recently returned from the Merryweather Multi-
city Canine Cavalcade with her dog, Bubblegum.
I’m afraid without more constant reenforcement,
even the best training gets forgot.
He leans across the desk and kisses Simone.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
You go away like that again, I might just
forget we got something goin’ on.
No such luck. You should know, neither
Bubblegum nor I are prone to bolting.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
That’s good. That’s very good.
(off him)
Sounds like there’s a story...
Emerson casually glances at the “Lil’ GumShoe” pop-up book on
top of some papers on his desk.
There was a story: Emerson had once fallen for
a woman who had bolted, and taken their baby
daughter to boot.
(picking it up)
Does it have to do with this book?
INSERT - PUSH IN ON THE LIL’ GUMSHOE POP-UP BOOK...
Emerson had written a pop-up book about his
missing daughter in hopes that, one day, he
would get it published and she would read it
and come find him.
Emerson reaches over and takes the book out of her hands and
drops it into his desk drawer, shutting it tight.
It’s nothin’.
She takes this in.
I realize what we have is still in the paper-
training phase. But we did agree to be honest
with each other.
I am being--
She CLICKS, he stops, she continues.
I like you. I am intensely optimistic about
our prospects. But you need to know that,
like any animal in a new situation, the thing
I hate the most is being surprised.
They hear someone CLEAR THEIR THROAT. Both Emerson and Simone
look up and STARTLE with a YELP to see:
AMELIA STINGWELL
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED: (2)
Well-dressed, matronly, 50s-60s, standing by the door.
Forgive me, but your door was ajar.
Just because it was ajar does not change the
fact that it was still a door before it was
ajar. Which would indicate to most people to
a-knock before a-entering.
(smiles)
How are you, Emerson?
Simone, this is Ms. Amelia Stingwell, sister
of Roland “Rollie” Stingwell, owner of the
Papen County Dam. I’d tell you more about
her, ‘cept for various reasons, we haven’t
spoken in nine years.
Those “various reasons” are dead now. Rollie
was killed last night.
I’m sorry for your loss.
I miss him terribly. He’d pop a vein if he
knew I was coming to you to solve his murder.
But you are the best in town.
(then)
Whoever killed Rollie must also have taken the
Dam Ruby. It’s gone.
“The damn ruby”?
The D-A-M, drop the “N,” Ruby. As in, a very
valuable precious stone dug up when they built
the dam.
He always wore it as a pendent. Never took it
off. Except to shower, and, I imagine, to
sleep. But that always muddles the story.
(to Emerson)
You find that ruby, and you’ll find Rollie’s
killer. After everything that went down all
those years ago, Emerson, I’d say it’s the
least you can do. Good day.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (3)
Amelia exits.
What happened between you and Rollie?
It’s nothin’.
As Simone SIGHS, annoyed...
The facts were these:
OFF this--

scenes.heading: INT. STINGWELL’S DAM OFFICE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Art Deco, well-appointed with a wall-sized map of the water pipe
system infrastructure under Papen County. ROLAND STINGWELL
stands behind his desk, gathering papers into his briefcase.
Roland “Rollie” Stingwell, millionaire builder
of the Papen County Dam and sole director of
the Papen County Water & Power department, was
last seen getting ready to leave after a busy
day at the office.
He takes out a RUBY PENDANT on a watch chain and gives it a
polish as his ASSISTANT, TRISH, enters to say good night.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His assistant said nothing seemed unusual, as
she said good night and headed out early for a
dinner engagement.
Trish leaves by the front door...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
What engagements engaged Rollie Stingwell in
the following hours were not known until the
next morning, when his body was discovered in
a dry riverbed one-half mile from the dam.
He exits out a PRIVATE ENTRANCE behind his desk and shuts the
door behind him.
OMIT
Chuck, Ned and Emerson stand over the sheet-covered body of
Rollie Stingwell.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
Thanks for coming down.
Emerson pulls back the sheet, REVEALING THE FRONT OF ROLLIE’S
BODY, WITH THE HEAD completely twisted 180 degrees FACEDOWN.
They react.
Oh, the poor man. And his poor head.
Ned touches the body, which SPARKS to life and sits up and swings
its legs around to face us (with his head now facing away). As
they walk around to the other side to speak with him...
Just think of him like an owl.
Who?
(giggles)
That was funny. He said, “Who?” Like an owl.
(to Emerson)
Why are you so quiet and grumpy?
How ya' doin’, Rollie?
Of all people, I didn’t expect to see you
here, Emerson Cod.
You know each other?
You might say we were affiliates. Affiliated
with a common third party.
There was nothing “common” about her and you
know it.
(re: Emerson)
He stole away the love of my life, and the
daffy thing is I paid him to do it. I trusted
you, Cod.
It ain’t stealin’ if the thing you’re stealin’
wants to be stolen.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED: (2)
I have questions.
(off his watch)
Which I will wait to ask.
Strange. I spent my life being angry about
this, but now, here in... uh...
A limbo-y non-denominational way station.
...the anger’s gone and I can see I spent my
life in the haze of a broken heart.
(quickly, to Emerson)
I don’t mean to step on toes, but shouldn’t
someone at this point ask him who did it?
Shhh.
(to Roland)
Go on...
I’ve tamed nature. I’ve stopped rivers from
flowing, but the one thing I could never do
was make that woman love me.
If it makes you feel any better, Stingwell,
neither could I.
It does make me feel better.
Who killed you, Stingwell?
Who do you think? It was Lila Robinson
herself. I assume she came back to steal
the ruby.
Man, I wish you’d said it was anyone else.
(checks his watch, re-deads)
Thank you for your time.
Who the heck is Lila Robinson?
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED: (3)
She’s the baby-mama that took my daughter.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
FADE IN:
OMIT
Emerson reads the paper, ignoring Ned and Chuck.
How could you not tell me about your
daughter? We’ve buried bodies together.
(joy)
You have a daughter. A daughter.
(to Ned)
And you knew this all along. How could you
not tell me?
(to Chuck)
You’re not fooling anyone.
(to Ned)
I know that any secret I tell you spends about
twenty seconds being secret before spilling
out into Dead Girl’s ears.
That is so not true.
It’s true.
It’s true. But I still can’t believe you didn’t
tell me. What about Simone? Does she know?
Emerson looks back, remains silent.
I’ll take that as a “no.”
As much as I’d love to ruminate on my painful
past while enjoying this slice of rhubarb? How
‘bout we find something else to chatter about.
Chuck looks at Ned...
What? Emerson shouldn’t feel any pressure to
divulge the hidden details of his hidden
past. It’s not like we’ve ever shared big
secrets with him...
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED:
Ned and Chuck stare at Emerson a beat, then:
It’s complicated.
What’s complicated about finding your baby-
stealing baby-mama and getting your daughter
back? We should be forming a posse right now.
“A posse”?
Okay, no posse. A small bunch. Us. If Lila
killed Roland Stingwell and stole the Dam
Ruby, then we’ve all just been hired to track
her down and find your daughter.
Chuck’s right. We could trace Stingwell’s
last steps. Maybe Lila left a trail behind.
I’ve spent the last seven years looking for
her and my kid. Lila’s a wily genius. A man-
eating, shape-shifting grifter who knows how
to get in, get out and vanish like heat off a
blacktop.
At least we could try. We need to try.
Maybe I could give it one more shot.
I don’t even know your daughter’s name.
Penny. My daughter’s name is Penny.
The facts were these: 9 years, 2 months, 14
days and 9 minutes earlier...

scenes.heading: INT. EMERSON’S OFFICE (9 YEARS AGO) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: A younger Emerson sits across from a client, a younger Rollie
Stingwell, who slides piles of cash across the desk.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
...Rollie Stingwell hired the P.I. to tail
his fiancée, Ms. Emily Von Alistair, an
arrestingly-beautiful woman who Rollie
suspected was having an affair.
As Stingwell hands Emerson a PHOTO of “EMILY” (LILA).

scenes.heading: EXT. RURAL ROAD - DAY (WB SWAMP ROAD) - FLASHBACK

lines.text: LILA ROBINSON is parked by the side of the road.
EMERSON
Watches from his car, with binoculars.
The affair, however, was with a dead man...
One Henry David Thoreau. And her furtive
trips away seemed to show only her desire for
a moment of solitude and ornithology to avoid
the hubbub of wedding planning.
EMERSON’S POV: THROUGH THE LEAVES--
She reads Walden.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But hiding from a bird-watcher in a Lincoln
Continental is not easy...
She turns her binoculars on him. Emerson sheepishly waves.

scenes.heading: INT. EMERSON’S CAR - WOODS - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Lila joins Emerson, hands him half her sandwich and a thermos.
...and so, Emily Von Alistair began sharing
her daily solitude, as well as her sandwich
and thermos of tomato soup. While
unconventional, Emerson reasoned he was still
very much keeping an eye on Emily.
TIME CUT:
Lila and Emerson have a picnic. He accepts his sandwich, can’t
help smiling back at her.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
With each passing thermos, the Private
Investigator grew more blind to the fact that
he was fast approaching the thin line between
stakeout... and make out.
He drops his sandwich in between them, they both lean in to get
it. They are staring in each other’s eyes very close...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Emerson hesitated, heeding not so much the
code of honor among men, as the “grody”
feeling one gets in a moment of weakness.
They both pull back from the almost-kiss.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But Emily had a solution, and that was to tell
the truth:
She begins talking.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Emerson Cod would discover that Emily was not
Emily. She was Lila Robinson, a grifter come
to town to play Stingwell for a fool. Her
aim, not to marry the millionaire, but to
divorce him of his famous Dam Ruby.
As they lean in, and kiss...

scenes.heading: INT. EMERSON’S OFFICE (9 YEARS AGO) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Emerson pushes a stack of CASH across his desk toward Rollie.
22 days later, the P.I. returned the money
Stingwell had paid him. What he could not
return...
Lila steps out of the shadows.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...was his client’s fiancée, or the new life
growing inside her.
PUSH IN on Lila to see the GLOWING IMAGE of a small fetus in her
belly. Stingwell jumps to his feet, irate.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Heartbroken and furious, Stingwell swore he’d be
watching. If the grifter ever grifted again,
he’d make sure she got put away for good.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED:
Stingwell scoops up his cash and storms out. Emerson turns to
Lila, who gazes up at him, frightened and grateful. Emerson
places a hand on her belly.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Lila promised to keep on the straight-and-
narrow...

scenes.heading: INT. STINGWELL’S OFFICE (9 YEARS AGO) - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Stingwell, at his desk, sketches a drawing of the schematic for
the pipe system.
...while Stingwell, relieved of the
distractions of a happy life, went on to build
Papen County Water & Power into a juggernaut.
Establishing. Impressive. Digital.
START on a YELLOWED PICTURE of ROLAND STINGWELL standing with
the DAM behind him, proudly holding up the RUBY as SEVERAL
WORKERS with shovels look on.
Find the Mod Squad looking around the tour lobby with Art Deco
fixtures and WPA-style works of art.
If we’re gonna find Lila, we need to retrace
Stingwell’s steps and figure out how his body
ended up half a mile away from here.
A TOUR GUIDE, a perky young man in blazer and badge, steps up.
Welcome to the Papen County Dam, source of
Papen County’s Water & Power. My name is
Taylor Philbean and, should you choose to take
a tour of this historic landmark and working
utility, I’ll be your dam guide.
(then)
When there’s a bigger group, this is where I
wait for the laugh to die down.
Actually, we’re invited guests of the
Stingwell family, here on the matter of Roland
Stingwell’s untimely death.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
Damn sad is what it is. If you’ll wait here
while I get your visitor passes, I’ll take you
up to his private office.
As he moves off to get some passes...
You said Lila chose to leave behind her life
of crime.
What happened?
People’s nature’s like a river. You can only
dam it up for so long. One day, she packed
her bags, broke back into Stingwell’s mansion
and when she couldn’t get the ruby, stole
fifty grand in cash. She knew he’d chase her
to the ends of the Earth, so she took Penny
and they disappeared into the night.
The guide returns, handing them paper passes.
If you’ll follow me...
They step through into a--
PHOTO STATION
Where families can pose in front of a “PAPEN COUNTY DAM - THE
BEST DAMN DAM AROUND” big foam backdrop of the dam.
You knew who Lila was. Did you really not see
it coming?
Guess I was blinded.
Say, “Cheese!”
They look over as--
FLASH! The automatic camera snaps a picture.
ANGLE ON THE PHOTOGRAPH DISPLAY UNIT nearby, a microfiche-like
roller with view screen, where we see Chuck, Ned and Emerson
caught by surprise in the touristy photo.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED: (2)
(to the guide)
Does this camera automatically take every
visitor’s picture?
Yes, for security reasons, should you be
planning to blow up the dam and flood the
valley, one copy is kept on file and another
is available for purchase as a keepsake in our
gift shop on the way out.
OFF this--
Stingwell’s assistant, Trish, 50s-60s, prim and quick, wearing
gloves, looks at a tourist photo booth PHOTOGRAPH of LILA in a
long dress and heels. [NOTE: there should be a vase of flowers
from Brunt’s farm somewhere on Stingwell’s big desk.]
You seen this woman before?
Name’s Lila Robinson. This photo was taken of
her entering the building the same day your
boss was killed.
I remember the woman. She did have a private
meeting with Mr. Stingwell, but I believe she
said her name was Marybeth Acres. The police
have already been here asking questions.
They ask you about... Marybeth?
No. They were asking about the multimillion-
dollar contracts Mr. Stingwell was negotiating
to replace all the old pipes that bring water
into the city.
I’d say the police are on the wrong track.
I agree. I tried to tell them my theory, but
they weren’t interested.
(conspiratorial)
I’m pretty sure this murder has to do with an
ongoing legal action I vigorously encouraged
Mr. Stingwell to pursue.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
Really?
I caught a local factory dumping toxic
chemicals into the dam reservoir at night.
And you blew the whistle? You go, girl.
(rational)
It’s my duty as a citizen to watch the
reservoir. We are 90 percent water, after
all. And just one drop of certain mind-
altering drugs, and we’ll all be zombies under
the control of those secret signals on the FM
radio. It’s a public health issue.
Emerson looks at Ned and Chuck, then turns and notes Stingwell’s
door.
What’s this door, here?
Mr. Stingwell’s private exit. It leads back
through the inside of the dam to a private
stairwell.
Emerson exits out the private door...
TRISH (CONT’D)
(to Ned and Chuck)
Do you care that I have important information?

OFF this--
We HEAR DRIPPING as Emerson walks down the spooky, windowless,

PUGET (O.S.)

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 22.
CONTINUED:
LT. DETECTIVE LAWRENCE PUGET, 30-40, steps out of the shadows.
Detective Puget. Been awhile.
Figured the Stingwells would hire a private

Being cocky in a cheap suit’s less effective

Who didn’t want to knock off Stingwell? You

Emerson hands Puget the photo of Lila.
Never known you to share, Cod. What’s your

My angle’s my angle. But maybe I wouldn’t mind

Don’t matter if said hammer happens to be

(a beat)
I do not.
Catch the bitch.
(then)
Use everything you got and move quickly,
‘cause I guaran-dam-tee you she’s moving fast

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 23.
Olive sits with Randy.
Thank you for coming back.
Sure.
First off, I just want to say I’m sorry if it

I guess I was a little surprised.
Signals are like nuts -- mixed is better. Who

Can I ask you a question? You’re not planning
to just use me to get over Ned, are you?
Sometimes, things are so absurd and far from the

If you’re not ready, I get that. But I’ve

There it is again...
(listens)
Nothing.
OFF this--
Emerson enters to find Simone waiting for him calmly in his chair.
Simone? How’d you get in?
There’s something I gotta tell you.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 24.
CONTINUED:
(rushing)
There’s something I gotta tell you, too. And
I feel bad ‘cause it’s gonna seem like I’m

Emerson, may I go first?
Sure.
I’m sorry.
Why are you sorry?
LILA STEPS OUT from behind Emerson...
Long time, no see, honey.
She flashes a small handgun, shuts the door.
Lila...
OFF this--
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 25.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. EMERSON’S OFFICE - NIGHT (PICKING UP FROM ACT TWO)

lines.text: Lila flashes a small handgun, shuts the door (as before).
Lila...
“Lila”? She told me her name was Priscilla
Saltpeter. Said she’d shoot me if I let on

She’s told lots of people lots of things.
(to Lila)
You in town to see a dead man about a ruby?
I’m in town to see you. And you really ought

Simone simmers, watching her.

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 26.
CONTINUED:
Penny’s the price I paid for thinking with my
heart instead of my head.
Penny is my daughter. It’s what I was going
to tell you.
(then, guiltily)
Surprise.
Simone falls silent, processing this...
I’ll give you 48 hours.
She’s lying to you. It’s in her eyes.
She’s lied so much in her life, her eyes are

(to Lila)
What’s to stop me from taking that toy gun and
pushing your delicate frame back through my
office wall?
Xylazine.
Come again?
Lila blows a fog of dust from a cigarette-sized tube into their
faces. As they pass out...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - LATER

lines.text: Ned, Chuck and Simone are at a booth.
It was horse tranquilizer. When we woke up,
Emerson made sure I was okay, then took off.
Said he was gonna start with all the angry
farmers, find out who the real killer was.
But we know who the real killer is. The dead

(to Simone)
Insofar as a dead man could tell us anything

If Lila has Penny, she holds all the cards.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 27.
CONTINUED:
We don’t even know for sure if Lila has his
daughter. She could be lying about that, too.
(then)
She’s playing him. Dominating his will to the
point he’s no longer listening to his instincts.
You don’t dominate Emerson. You really think

He wouldn’t do that. That’s not who he is.
What if “who he is” isn’t who he is right now?
And maybe, instead of analyzing him, we should

(stands to go)
Forgive me, but if helping Emerson means we

then I won’t be part of it. Someone backs you
into a corner, you don’t get obedient. You

Simone, wait...
All I asked from him was that we start out
with honesty and no surprises. I would say

And she exits. Chuck tries to follow. Olive steps up to Ned.
Is this a bad time to talk? ‘Cause I just
wanted to say I’m pretty sure Randy’s gonna do
the trick, you know, wiping the emotional slate
clean. He’s picking me up after work tonight.
(distracted)
That’s great, Olive.
See, soon I’ll be the one lost in some
distracty thought, not caring, while you
prattle on about your relationship problems.
I’m sorry. I do care, and I am distracty.
(then)
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 28.
CONTINUED: (2)
Olive, hypothetically, if you and I had a
love child, but I’d been a criminal all my
life and then when our daughter was one and a
half I kidnapped her and disappeared for
seven years, then came back and asked you to
prove I didn’t commit a murder that I almost
certainly did commit--
Yes, I will! I will! A year and a half is
better than nothing, and even if you take the
kid, I’ll know we had it together and I’ll
love it forever and whoever you have to kill,
I’m sure you have a good reason, and you said
“hypothetically”--
(catching herself, calmly)
So, I dunno. Maybe. What was the question?
Can love make you do something absolutely crazy?
I went. To a nunnery.
Thank you. And have a great time tonight.
He finds Chuck, down the way...
NED (CONT’D)
You’re right. If Emerson’s desperate enough
not to see the truth, then he’s desperate
enough to do anything.
He needs us.
Let’s go.
As they quickly exit out the front door and INTO CAMERA...
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 29.
A greenhouse with flower farmland beyond. CRICKETS. BREEZE.
It was the end of a long day, and Emerson,
Chuck and the Pie-Maker had interviewed 28
disgruntled farmers, concluding that, due to
various circumstances, none were guilty of the
murder of Roland Stingwell.
As we MOVE IN past flowers...
This was not a surprising fact, as Roland
Stingwell had already told them that it was
Lila Robinson who had killed him. What was
surprising was that, in spite of this, Emerson
Cod insisted on moving on to farmer number 29.
We find our Mod Squad with MICHAEL BRUNT, flower farmer.
Mr. Brunt, you had two hundred acres of
riverfront farmland till they built the dam,
isn’t that right?
If this were my flower farm, I’d be all thorns
and no rose when it came to Mr. Stingwell.
My farm used to be the most prosperous in the
county. Now with what I pay to truck in
water, I can barely pay the rent, same as
everybody else that stayed. But what else
would I do?
(to Chuck)
When is your birthday, precious?
November.
Brunt holds a vase of flowers up to Chuck...
Funny. I would have bet you were an autumn
birthday. The deep orange of orchid embers
and Asiatic lilies makes your skin tone glow.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 30.
CONTINUED:
I have two birthdays, actually. And my second
is in the fall, so actually, you’re right.
Your gibberish is sweet, honey. Keep the flowers.
I’m telling the truth.
Well, so am I. If I’d killed Stingwell, I
suppose I would have done it years ago, when
my anger was fresh-cut. But nothing’s gonna
change. Whoever has the water has the power.
They exit, Chuck carrying the vase of flowers. Ned and Chuck do
their best to play hopeful and energetic...
Seems like most of the anger around here’s
gotten as dry and dusty as the riverbed.
Angry farmer angle’s getting thin.
What about the contracts to re-pipe the

As Emerson heads for the car...
Nah. Stingwell was behind the plan, but the

out the construction, so there’s no motive.
(then, sadly)
We got nothin’.
Chuck and Ned look at a broken Emerson, then at each other.
What about the big-business polluter angle?
Don’t be humoring me. If you didn’t think we
were out of leads and I was high on Lila-berry
juice, what would you call the “big-business
polluter angle”?
I might call it “that crazy conspiracy theory
from Stingwell’s crazy assistant.”
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 31.
CONTINUED:
Or “the last-ditch crackpot angle,” for short.
But it’s something...
Emerson gets his mojo back, heads for the car...
Well, it’s all we got left. And we’re running
out of time.
Ned and Chuck exchange a look, then follow.
Chuck, Ned and Emerson (in between) sit across from THREE FAST-
TALKING LAWYERS.
We appreciate you coming in to talk to us on
such short notice. We’re investigating the
death of Roland Stingwell.
His assistant said there was a heated legal

the Fits and Giggles Novelty Company.

the fact that your client’s factory was

These are baseless allegations.
Our client did not, nor would they, ever
dispose of any kind of chemical into the
reservoir. This is a categorical denial--
Maybe once.
And one time only.
Once. We may have inadvertently allowed a

But it was a long time ago.
It was Tuesday.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.
CONTINUED:
Very, very early Tuesday. Nearly Monday.
What kind of lawyers are you?
We are Mennonites. Which would not normally

But to be clear: In regards to the chemicals
that were or were not--
Were.
--dumped in the reservoir at an indeterminate
time--
Last Tuesday.
Two a.m.-ish.
Two-thirty-nine in the morning.
There was a spill.
That’s the truth.
Our plastics division had an overflow. But it

Pure drinking water with chemicals in it.
Abner’s beaten.
We will pay the fine to the appropriate

OFF this--
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 33.

The lawyers are exiting. Emerson, Ned and Chuck talk.
They’re polluters, but they’re no killers.
Every road’s a dead end.

No, we can’t.
The police are gonna go down that road.

Let’s say the police do find Lila? What’s to

Emerson exits as Olive steps up.
(notices)

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 34.
CONTINUED:

(then)
Oh my gosh.
(lump in throat)

OFF Chuck and Ned, been there before--

OLIVE (O.S.)
Emerson? Are you here? I just heard about

She opens the unlocked door and enters. A RED LANTERN FLASHES

SIMONE (CONT’D)
We gotta talk.

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 35.
FADE IN:

Witch.

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 36.

I did grow a conscience. She’s sitting in a

(then)
And evil.
(to Simone)
Right?

OLIVE (CONT’D)

OLIVE (CONT’D)

LISTEN to Lila run down the stairs and out the door. Then:

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 37.
CONTINUED: (2)

See if you can follow them in your van. I

Lila gets in HER CAR, starts the engine, puts it in gear. PUSH
IN ON THE TRUNK AS NED REACHES OUT FROM INSIDE, SHUTTING IT.
Unaware that Chuck and the Pie-Maker were

...the desperate investigator returned one

PUGET (CONT’D)
Lila Robinson, aka, Sheila Slapikoff, aka,

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 38.

(heading away)
Thanks for the tip, Cod. And don’t worry. If

Emerson watches Puget walk off into the shadows.
At that moment, Emerson Cod was overcome with
the 100% certainty that he would never see his
daughter again. And then...
Emerson looks at the picture of Lila on the machine, then up at a

Every Drop Counts!” (like the one in Stingwell’s office).
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...he was un-overcome by an idea that had a 1%
chance of being correct.
As his eyes narrow.
Hey, now...
SIMONE (O.S.)
Emerson.
He turns, brightens.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 39.
CONTINUED: (2)
Simone.
I knew you’d return to the scene of the crime.
I’m sorry I bolted on you.
You’re back now.
(then)
Come with me.
They exit through the photo station, setting off the FLASH--
As the private eye set off to test his new
theory for leaks...
WE COME OVER THE TOP OF LILA.
...the tall drink of water driving into the

PUSH IN ON THE TRUNK, where the metal DISSOLVES transparent and
we see inside to--
Ned and Chuck, packed like sardines, her head to his feet and

If love does make you stupid, then we really
must love Emerson.
If we find Penny, this will be worth it.
They bump along in the semi-darkness. Then:
CHUCK (CONT’D)
Ned?
Yes.
Were we stupid to fall in love?
We didn’t choose it. It happened.
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 40.
CONTINUED:
I know I said our love was hearty, but that’s
just another way of saying it’s hard.
No more than other people.
(then)
Okay, maybe a little more than other people.
When you let me live more than a minute, you
said you didn’t have a choice, but you did.
We tell ourselves we don’t have a choice to
fall in love, but we do -- and if Emerson
hadn’t been blinded by love, then he never
would have had Penny, and he wouldn’t have
anything to lose. Which would have been so
much easier.
Do you want us to be easier?
I dunno. Maybe there’s exhaust fumes. But why
love something, if loving something means you do
stupid things and just have more to lose?
“Why love something?”
(then)
Because we can.
Misty-eyed, Chuck breaks into a big smile, hugs Ned’s feet. The
car BUMPS to a QUICK STOP. They HEAR a car door open, then look:
OUT THE TRUNK
At Lila.
In my experience, if you’re hiding in a trunk,
it’s a good idea not to chat.
OFF this--
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 41.
FADE IN:
Closed for business. Olive and Randy enter, excited.
How could you lose them?
They were three blocks ahead. I wasn’t
comfortable jumping the curb.
Ned and Chuck are okay, right? I mean, they
have to be.
(steady, reassuring)
Yeah. You did disarm the crazy-ass she-wolf.
(then)
Is it insensitive of me to say this is fun?
Only if they’re dead. Which they’re not,
right? They’re fine.
(then)
Can I be honest with you? If you could read
my mind -- which I’m glad you can’t, but it
doesn’t matter because I’m going to tell you
anyway--
When?
Now. You were right. I did want to use you
to squeeze the feelings I have for Ned out of
my head. But I don’t think I can do that.
I like you, Olive. I like spending time with
you.
That’s the problem. I don’t want that to make
you all muddle-headed so you make a bad
choice. I’ve been through a lot. I’m going
to be difficult.
I know it would be stupid to be your rebound
guy.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 42.
CONTINUED:
But I also think, maybe, after a while, you’ll
forget you ever bounced. And I’m willing to
take that chance.
Maybe if we’re careful, there’s a way to do it
smart so that neither of us get hur--
He kisses her.
How was that?
That was brilliant.
He holds her. She closes her eyes...
OLIVE (CONT’D)
For the first time... in a very long time, the
thoughts I had of Ned are gone from my head...
(then, noticing)
...and standing outside the door.
TAP-TAP at the door. Randy turns around to see:
Ned, in his underwear, outside. He enters.
(calling out behind)
Clearing...
Ned steps out of the way as Chuck enters, also shivering in a
slip...
C... c... crossing.
What happened?
Lila caught us, took our clothes and left us
by the side of the road.
Randy, can you pull your car around? We’ll

Sure.
We gotta find Emerson. Who knows what Lila

PUSHING DAISIES #212 "Water & Power" 10/21/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 43.
CONTINUED: (2)
Olive and Randy head for the front. Ned HITS THE LIGHTS AS HE
PASSES TO THE KITCHEN. CAMERA STAYS IN THE DARK PIE HOLE FOR A
MOMENT. The FLOWERS in the VASE from the flower farmer are
GLOWING.
Ned, Chuck, Olive and Randy rush back, leaning into the glow.
Why are these flowers glowing in the dark?
We need to get to the dam.
OFF this--
Emerson and Simone enter the dark office. We see that the
FLOWERS ON STINGWELL’S DESK are also GLOWING.
I knew it.
He flips on the LIGHTS and goes straight to a vase of flowers.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
These are from Michael Brunt’s farm.
Delivered on the day Stingwell died.
Were they glowing in the dark?
He moves to the transparent map of “PAPEN COUNTY PROPER” on the
wall.
We know Stingwell was about to approve a
multimillion-dollar renovation of the water
pipes from the dam reservoir to the city, right?
(grabs map from wall)
